text.label: Text: You have heard it your whole career: the
text.value: You have heard it your whole career: the money is in the list, and you are in the relationship business. You believe it, and that is exactly why it stings. Somewhere in your email list, your DMs and your old student records is every person who ever raised their hand, and almost none of them have heard from you since. Not because you stopped caring. Because staying in touch with all of them, every day, is not something a human being can do.

text.label: Text: It sounds like a computer word, so most peop…
text.value: It sounds like a computer word, so most people stop listening. It is not one. Your database is every person who ever raised their hand: the one who downloaded your guide in March, the student from two summers ago, the DM you never got back to, the reader who emailed after the book and never heard from you again.

text.label: Text: It is sitting in three or four places right …
text.value: It is sitting in three or four places right now: your email list, your DMs, a spreadsheet somebody made, and whatever checkout or course software you sold through. You have one whether or not you ever called it that. Every name in it is a relationship you already started and never finished.

text.label: Text: Every name in there cost you something t
text.value: Every name in there cost you something to get. Ad money, a guide you gave away, years of videos, an hour of your evening answering DMs. That effort is spent and gone. The person is still there, and they still know who you are.

text.label: Text: A brand-new stranger costs you that same mon…
text.value: A brand-new stranger costs you that same effort all over again, and they trust you less than the one who already raised their hand once. Working the people who already know you is the only marketing where the expensive part is behind you. Everybody who teaches marketing says this on day one. Almost nobody is given a way to actually do it.

text.label: Text: The old way was memory. A notebook, a card f…
text.value: The old way was memory. A notebook, a spreadsheet, a note that says write back to her, and a promise to yourself that you will get to everybody. That works when you know forty people. You have not known only forty people for a long time.

text.label: Text: Say the list is two thousand. Doing it the w…
text.value: Say the list is two thousand. Doing it the way you were taught means a real message to each one, then a reply to whatever comes back, then a sale or a booked call, nights and weekends included, because that is when people answer. Then again next month, and the month after. You do not have that time and neither does your team, so it never happens. That is not a character flaw. It is the job being bigger than the day, and it is why the list quietly ages out while everyone agrees to stop thinking about it.
